questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: Shift down one gear at a time. Release the clutch slowly between each shift.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should ride:

options.text: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position makes you more visible.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle:

options.text: You may exceed the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You may ignore "No passing zone" markings if you started in a passing zone.
You may pass on the shoulder.
You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in legal passing zones.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stay within the speed limit and pass only in legal passing zones.
questions.explanation: Always pass within the speed limit and only where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: A good way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Honk your horn or make rude gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up will only cause them to follow at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: Keep your motorcycle upright and move slowly across slippery surfaces.

questions.question: Which surface provides the best traction for a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Dry pavement provides the best traction. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, lane markings, and metal covers all reduce traction.

questions.question: Which color is best to wear to be seen while riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Orange
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green. Bright clothing makes you easier to see, day or night.

questions.question: An approved helmet should:

options.text: Allow you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A Department of Transportation-approved helmet allows you to see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: If stopping will take longer than usual, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, increase your following distance. This gives you more room to stop if needed.

questions.question: When choosing footwear for riding, select:

options.text: Shoes with long laces that hang out.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be short. Laces should be tucked in so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces reduce tire grip. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, oil, and metal covers are all more dangerous than dry pavement for motorcyclists.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Ride it like your own bike, since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Each motorcycle is different. Check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes a few times first.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
Only use your mirrors to see your surroundings.
Point in the direction you want to change.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Mirrors alone are not enough.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to handle differently while riding, you should:

options.text: Pull over and check the tires.
Pull over and check the chain.
Pull over and check the windshield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the tires.
questions.explanation: A sudden change in handling usually means a tire has failed. If you feel your motorcycle handling differently, pull over safely and check your tires.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may pull out unexpectedly into your path.
Other drivers may go slowly looking for a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may pull out unexpectedly into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver might pull out without looking. Car doors might open into your lane. Pedestrians might step out between cars.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: The shortest and safest stops use both the front and rear brakes smoothly and gradually, without skidding either tire.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Follow the vehicle ahead as closely as possible.
Look only at your controls, not ahead.
Signal your intentions to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal your intentions to other drivers.
questions.explanation: To prevent crashes, stay visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and look ahead, behind, and to the sides.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if it finishes before another vehicle comes.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: You cannot pass in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Skip the jacket if it is warm.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: For protection, always wear a long-sleeved jacket, even in warm weather. A jacket helps prevent dehydration. Always wear long pants and tuck in shoelaces so they do not catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: It is best to not ride directly alongside another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be in its blind spot.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be hard to see what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to a vehicle is dangerous because you may be in the vehicle's blind spot. The driver will not know you are there. It is also dangerous because the vehicle may block your escape route if another hazard appears.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and bright clothing when riding a motorcycle. Crashes happen day and night. Wear highly visible clothing at all times.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stocking cap
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. Good protective gear includes sturdy jackets and pants that cover your arms and legs, boots that cover and support your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Front and rear
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you change lanes
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes. Do this even if you think no one is around to see it.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals. When your left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means you plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: Before riding, you should check everything except:
questions.correctAnswerText: The seat fabric
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. Check the rims and spokes for bends or damage. Check tire condition and tread. Check all lights.

questions.question: How can you prevent injury on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce your speed. Sudden moves can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to escape a slippery road.

questions.question: Is riding at night easier or harder than riding during the day?

options.text: Easier because you can see other vehicles' lights better
Harder because it is harder to see
Less distracting than riding during the day

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder because it is harder to see
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because you cannot see as well as during the day. Poor light makes it hard to judge distances and see clearly.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black lettering
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What should you do when riding with a passenger?

options.text: Squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more distance to stop. Ride slower, start slowing sooner, leave more space between cars, and wait for larger gaps in traffic.
